summary: Iteration 6 executed the full Group A backend test plan (Order Lifecycle & Editing) end-to-end via pytest against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_6_order_lifecycle.py covering all 14 scenarios in the review request. RESULT: 19/19 pytest tests PASS. The 13 newly-added PATCH allowed_fields all persist and appear in changed_fields. Super Admin can edit after is_ready=true; outlet_admin gets 400 with the exact detail 'Cannot edit order after it\'s marked as ready. Contact Super Admin.'. total_amount PATCH recalculates pending_amount = total - paid and normalize_pending zeroes dust <1. Activity log entries with action_type=order_updated contain non-empty before_data + after_data. secondary_images list of 5 URLs persists exactly. Super-admin direct delete and outlet-admin-request → approve-delete flow both store deleted_from_status and deleted_from_lifecycle_status. GET /api/orders/deleted returns an array (route not shadowed by /orders/{order_id}). WhatsAppTemplateEvent.ORDER_UPDATED enum works — server started cleanly and PATCH succeeds even though AiSensy config is absent (send_whatsapp_notification silently returns False, background task doesn't propagate).

minor.issue: Endpoint has no server-side filter for entity_id/order_id — the review request suggested filtering by entity_id. Tests currently filter client-side after fetching action_type=order_updated. Consider adding an entity_id query param for large activity_logs collections.

Response body is {message, order_id, order_number, lifecycle_status, ...} — NOT the full order object and NOT a top-level 'id' field. This is inconsistent with other resource POSTs (e.g., POST /api/users returns UserResponse). Frontend callers must know to use order_id, not id. Consider standardising to return the full Order object.

There is NO direct GET-by-id endpoint for orders. To verify a PATCH, callers must scan /api/orders/manage or /orders/hold or /orders/pending. This makes UI refresh flows and testing awkward. Consider adding GET /api/orders/{order_id}.

test_coverage_results.2_outlets_fetch: PASS — /api/outlets returns list. Fixture auto-seeds an outlet when db is empty (needed on fresh preview env).
test_coverage_results.3_create_hold_order: PASS — POST /api/orders?is_punch_order=false with full valid payload returns 200 + order_id + lifecycle_status='active' (all required fields present so it goes active, not hold — this is per current backend logic).
test_coverage_results.4_patch_13_allowed_fields: PASS — receiver_info, delivery_address, delivery_city, zone_id, needs_delivery, outlet_id, order_taken_by, is_hold, lifecycle_status, status, delivery_charge, custom_delivery_charge, voice_instruction_url all update, appear in changed_fields, and persist on subsequent GET.
test_coverage_results.5_pending_recalc_normalize: PASS — total_amount=paid+1234 → pending=1234.00. total_amount=paid+0.4 → pending=0.0 (normalize_pending zeroed the dust <1).
test_coverage_results.6_super_admin_edit_after_ready: PASS — After POST /api/orders/{id}/mark-ready (is_ready=true), super admin PATCH still returns 200.
test_coverage_results.7_non_super_blocked_after_ready: PASS — outlet_admin PATCH after is_ready=true → 400 with detail exactly 'Cannot edit order after it\'s marked as ready. Contact Super Admin.'
test_coverage_results.8_activity_log_persistence: PASS — GET /api/activity-logs?action_type=order_updated returns entries; at least one entry for the target order has non-empty before_data + after_data (diff snapshots).
test_coverage_results.9_whatsapp_bg_task_tolerant: PASS — PATCH still 200s despite AiSensy config absent (send_whatsapp_notification silently returns False when config missing — verified via successful PATCHes throughout the suite).
test_coverage_results.10_secondary_images_5_urls: PASS — PATCH secondary_images=['/uploads/a.jpg'..'/uploads/e.jpg'] → GET returns exactly the same 5 URLs in order.
test_coverage_results.11_super_delete_stores_pre_status: PASS — DELETE /api/orders/{id}?reason=test-delete as super_admin → GET /api/orders/deleted → entry has deleted_from_status + deleted_from_lifecycle_status matching pre-delete values.
test_coverage_results.12_non_super_delete_then_approve: PASS — outlet_admin DELETE creates pending request (200), super_admin POST /approve-delete succeeds, /orders/deleted entry has both deleted_from_* fields matching pre-delete values.
test_coverage_results.13_deleted_route_not_shadowed: PASS — GET /api/orders/deleted returns a JSON array (route resolves ahead of any /orders/{order_id} pattern).
test_coverage_results.14_enum_startup_sanity: PASS — ORDER_UPDATED added to WhatsAppTemplateEvent enum; server started cleanly and authenticated endpoints work.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Add GET /api/orders/{order_id} to make the resource RESTful and simplify frontend refresh / audit flows.

OPTIONAL: Standardise POST /api/orders to return the full Order object (with 'id') instead of the current {message, order_id, order_number, ...} envelope. Would remove the id vs order_id inconsistency callers hit today.
OPTIONAL: Add entity_id (or order_id) query filter to GET /api/activity-logs — the current filter set does not include it, so tests / audit UIs must pull all logs and filter client-side.

OPTIONAL: PATCH /api/orders/{id} allowed_fields does not include is_ready or ready_at. If a super admin needs to un-ready an order via PATCH, they currently can't (they'd have to use direct DB or a new endpoint). mark-ready is one-way (raises 400 if already ready).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 6649 lines — WAY over the 700-line guideline. Refactor into routers/orders.py, routers/auth.py, routers/reports.py, routers/whatsapp.py, etc. This is the single biggest maintenance risk in the codebase.

PATCH /api/orders/{id} now allows editing outlet_id, lifecycle_status, and status directly through a generic dict. There is NO validation that outlet_id refers to a real outlet, or that lifecycle_status/status values are members of the enums. A super-admin (or a compromised super-admin token) can leave orders in impossible states like status='chocolate'. Consider Pydantic OrderUpdate model or explicit whitelists per field.

PATCH /api/orders/{id} recalculates pending_amount only when total_amount OR delivery_charge is in the payload — but total_amount and delivery_charge are stored as separate concepts, and total_amount is documented as 'cake+delivery already'. If a caller PATCHes ONLY delivery_charge (leaving total_amount alone), pending_amount is recalculated using the existing total_amount (which already contains delivery_charge), producing a stale/wrong pending. Confirm the invariant and unit-test the delivery_charge-only PATCH path.

activity-logs endpoint response includes before_data/after_data as raw dicts. If a field like receiver_info contains PII, this is now stored in an audit table indefinitely and exposed to any super_admin. Consider redacting known PII fields (phone, address) or masking in the response.

DELETE /api/orders/{order_id} allows FACTORY_MANAGER as a delete-requester (line 2485). approve-delete restricts to SUPER_ADMIN. But the current UI/tests only exercise SUPER_ADMIN + OUTLET_ADMIN. Confirm FACTORY_MANAGER also creates a pending request (not direct delete) — the code path looks correct but is not test-covered.

DELETE /api/orders/{id} for non-super role sets delete_status='pending' but does NOT record the delete_requested_by user or reason (wait — line 2523 does record both). However, if the same order already had a rejected prior request, a fresh DELETE from a non-super OVERWRITES the previous delete_reason with no audit — the reject-delete path (line 2570) already clears them, so this is OK, but worth adding a test for the rejected→re-requested flow.

TestActivityLog: server does not accept entity_id as a query param on /api/activity-logs (see line 6608 signature). Test filters client-side, which will get slow on large activity_logs collections. Add the filter.

TestNonSuperBlockedAfterReady covers the 400 message. But note: outlet_admin was auto-created with role='outlet_admin' via POST /api/users. If the schema for UserCreate ever changes required outlet fields, this fixture will break — consider seeding via a fixtures.py helper.

POST /api/orders returns 'lifecycle_status':'active' for a payload that has ALL of {customer, phone, delivery_date/time, flavour, cake_image_url, total>0} — matching the is_complete check at line 2208. The review calls this a HOLD order because is_hold could be true; the backend distinguishes 'hold' by lifecycle_status='hold' when is_complete is false. Semantics confusion — worth documenting in server.py which fields are truly required for a non-hold order.

seed_data_creation: Fresh preview DB had zero outlets — outlet_id fixture now auto-seeds one 'TEST Outlet <hex>' before running order tests. Also seeds one outlet_admin user per session. All test-created customers/orders use 'TEST' prefix for easy cleanup. NOT cleaning up after run so the created data is auditable in the next iteration; caller can drop TEST_* users and set is_deleted=true orders manually if desired.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All Group A backend changes are green. To re-run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_6_order_lifecycle.py -v`. The 3 minor backend observations (no GET /orders/{id}, POST /orders response shape uses order_id not id, activity-logs has no entity_id filter) are quality-of-life improvements, not blockers — flag them to main agent as OPTIONAL. If frontend is later tested against these backend changes, verify that Orders.jsx / OrderEdit.jsx read 'order_id' (not 'id') from the create response, and that Activity Logs UI has some way to filter by order (currently client-side only via action_type filter).
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no bugs found. Only cosmetic / API-shape observations.
